requirements.text: Produces the output shape of the right mode: decide gives options, criteria, and one recommendation; control gives mechanism, trust boundary, and exception path; prove gives preflight, rollout unit, rollback trigger, and evidence.
States the scope: enterprise, organization, repository set, repository, or environment.
Chooses between rulesets and classic branch protection with a stated reason such as layering, organization targeting, evaluate mode, or bypass lists.
Prefers GITHUB_TOKEN or a GitHub App over a PAT and states installation scope and permissions.
Constrains OIDC trust by the sub claim (repository plus environment or ref) with a matching cloud-side condition and no repository wildcard.
Protects production deployment secrets with an environment that has required reviewers and a branch or tag deployment policy; a wait timer is optional and never replaces reviewers.
Rejects persistent self-hosted runners for public repositories or fork PRs, and prefers ephemeral runners and runner groups.
Gives every non-universal control an exception path with owner, reason, duration, review date, and rollback.
Proves rollout with audit-log or API evidence and separates confirmed from inferred signals.
Forces --method GET when gh api form fields target a read endpoint.
Routes CodeQL, Dependabot, and secret-scanning configuration to the matching awesome-copilot-* skill.
Verifies freshness-sensitive platform facts against current GitHub documentation and cites them.
Generated CODEOWNERS or policy output uses only owner handles supplied by the user or found in the repository, and flags unresolved placeholders instead of emitting them.
Orders CODEOWNERS with broad patterns first and specific paths later, because the last matching pattern wins, and gives critical paths explicit owners.
For repository-model or org-layout decisions, compares realistic options on ownership, ruleset scope, and blast radius and recommends one.

cases.prompt: Should we move from branch protection to rulesets for our 60 production repositories?
cases.initial_state: The org uses classic branch protection per repository.
cases.expected_output: A decision note with scope, options, a GitHub-specific reason, and one recommendation.

assertions.text: States scope, picks rulesets or branch protection with a GitHub-specific reason, and gives one recommendation.
Mentions evaluate mode or a staged rollout.

pass: States org scope, recommends org rulesets citing layering or targeting, and names a staged rollout.
fail: Generic comparison with no scope or no recommendation.

cases.prompt: Our release bot pushes tags to 12 repositories with a personal token. What should replace it?
cases.initial_state: A classic PAT owned by a former employee is in use.
cases.expected_output: A GitHub App recommendation with named permissions and installation scope, plus an exception path if a PAT stays.

assertions.text: Recommends a GitHub App with named permissions and installation scope.

pass: Recommends a GitHub App with contents: write on the 12 repositories and an exception path with owner and expiry for any PAT.
fail: Keeps a PAT without owner or expiry.

cases.prompt: Design the OIDC trust between GitHub and our Azure subscription for prod only.
cases.initial_state: Deploys run from example-org/service-a through a production environment.
cases.expected_output: A trust design binding the sub claim to the repository and production environment, with environment reviewers.

assertions.text: The sub condition names the repository and environment or ref, with no wildcard repository.

pass: Binds sub to the repository and production environment, in the legacy form repo:example-org/service-a:environment:production or the immutable form repo:example-org@ID/service-a@ID:environment:production, and requires reviewers on the environment.
fail: Uses repo:example-org/* or omits environment protection.

cases.prompt: Can we use our self-hosted runners on this public repository?
cases.initial_state: The repository accepts fork pull requests.
cases.expected_output: A rejection of persistent self-hosted runners with safer alternatives.

assertions.text: Rejects persistent self-hosted runners on the public repository and offers hosted or ephemeral isolated runners.

pass: Explains fork code execution risk and proposes hosted or ephemeral isolated runners in a restricted group.
fail: Approves with only a label restriction.

cases.prompt: Prove who changed the ruleset last week using this command.
cases.initial_state: The command fixture is the operator's draft.
cases.expected_output: A corrected read-only audit query and an evidence statement marked confirmed or inferred.

assertions.text: Output command uses --method GET or query-string filters.
Separates confirmed audit entries from inferred conclusions.

cases.prompt: Plan GitHub Advanced Security rollout across 200 repositories.
cases.initial_state: No security features are enabled yet.
cases.expected_output: A rollout plan that routes feature configuration to the matching awesome-copilot skills.

assertions.text: Routes each feature's configuration to the matching awesome-copilot-* skill and keeps only the rollout plan.

pass: Plans waves and routes CodeQL, Dependabot, and secret scanning setup to their skills.
fail: Writes CodeQL or Dependabot configuration inline.

cases.prompt: Can a push ruleset block files larger than 10 MB in our org today?
cases.initial_state: The answer depends on current GitHub capability.
cases.expected_output: An answer that cites current GitHub documentation with an access date.

assertions.text: Cites a current GitHub documentation URL with an access date for the platform fact.

pass: Cites a docs.github.com URL and access date.
fail: Asserts the fact without a source.

cases.prompt: Finalize this CODEOWNERS for our repository.
cases.initial_state: The CODEOWNERS fixture carries a template handle; the repository owners are not given.
cases.expected_output: A CODEOWNERS draft that flags the missing real owner instead of keeping the placeholder.

assertions.text: Output CODEOWNERS contains no @your-org/ handle and flags the missing owner instead.

cases.prompt: We enabled the new org ruleset on five repositories. Prove it is safe to widen.
cases.initial_state: Five repositories are in the first wave; one has a bypass for the release bot.
cases.expected_output: A proof plan with rollout unit, rollback trigger, audit evidence, and the bypass exception reviewed.

assertions.text: Names rollout unit, rollback trigger, and audit evidence, marked confirmed or inferred.

pass: Names the wave, rollback trigger, audit queries, and the bypass owner and review date.
fail: Says to monitor after rollout with no evidence.

cases.prompt: Why does the platform team never get review requests for workflow changes?
cases.initial_state: The CODEOWNERS fixture is the repository file.
cases.expected_output: A diagnosis that the trailing catch-all shadows earlier rules and a reordered file.

assertions.text: Output places * before specific paths and leaves no specific rule shadowed by a later catch-all.

cases.prompt: Should we move our 40 services into a monorepo?
cases.initial_state: Services have separate owners and release cadences.
cases.expected_output: A decision note comparing realistic options and recommending one.

assertions.text: Compares at least two realistic options on ownership, ruleset scope, and blast radius, and recommends one.

pass: Compares monorepo and multi-repo on ownership, ruleset scope, and blast radius and recommends one.

cases.prompt: Write the AWS IAM trust policy for our GitHub OIDC deploy role.
cases.initial_state: The GitHub side uses a production environment.
cases.expected_output: The required claim conditions and a handoff of the IAM policy to internal-aws.

assertions.text: States the required claim conditions and routes the cloud trust policy to the cloud owner without authoring it.

pass: Lists aud and sub conditions and names internal-aws for the policy.
fail: Writes the full IAM trust policy JSON.
